reasons: Classification is correct: Article XIII(b) caps only Licensor at one half of amounts paid and leaves Licensee uncapped (aggravated by the one-way Article XII indemnity with no super-cap), which is squarely walk-away territory under LOL-CAP, well short of the mutual 12-months'-fees fallback.

Redline is actionable and reaches the playbook position with a targeted rewrite: subsection (a) is made mutual ('EITHER PARTY ... THE OTHER PARTY'), subsection (b) is replaced with a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, an Excluded Claims definition supplies the required carve-outs (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and Licensee's fee obligations are excluded from capped damages.

The advisory high changed-character ratio on the second operation is expected here — the rule requires replacing the one-sided cap sentence outright; the rest of the Article (including subsection (c)) is left intact.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice: it states what changed, why (Licensor capped at half of fees while our liability was unlimited), that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap, and offers the straight mutual 12-month fee cap as fallback.

Note for the drafter (not a basis for failure): the retained sentence in (a) ('UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE ... FOR ANY ... INFRINGEMENT ...') sits in tension with the new IP-infringement carve-out and would ideally be conformed or addressed under the IP/indemnity rule.
